title: Update to U.S. Referral and Fulfillment by Amazon fees for 2026
claim: Amazon raised FBA fees by an average $0.08/unit effective 2026-01-15 after no 2025 increase; fee structures made more granular; no new fee types in 2026.
excerpt: FBA fees will increase by an average of $0.08 per unit sold, or less than 0.5% of an average item's selling price.
limitations: Average only; category-level tables are on login-gated Seller Central. Third-party reports of an April 2026 fuel/logistics surcharge (~3.5%) not verified from an Amazon primary source.

title: Selling on Amazon pricing (referral fees by category, selling plans)
claim: Professional plan $39.99/mo; referral fees: Beauty/Health & Personal Care and Baby 8% if <=$10 else 15%; Grocery 8% if <=$15 else 15%; Pet 15% (22% vet diets); Home & Kitchen 15%; Toys 15%; Clothing 5%/10%/17% tiered by price; $0.30 minimum in most categories.
excerpt: Beauty, Health and Personal Care: 8% for total sales price of $10.00 or less; 15% above $10.00 (paraphrased table).
limitations: Public marketing page; FBA fulfillment fee tables not shown; no effective date displayed.

organization: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (Federal Register 2026-12670)
title: Indefinite suspension of the de minimis exemption for merchandise arriving through all modes other than international mail
claim: CBP interim final rule indefinitely suspends the $800 de minimis exemption for all non-postal shipments from all countries; companion rule 2026-12669 covers international mail.
excerpt: Indefinite suspension of the de minimis exemption for merchandise arriving through all modes other than international mail (title).
limitations: Interim final rule; postal effective-date details differ across secondary summaries. Separate statutory repeal scheduled for 2027 not re-verified here.

title: Continuing the Suspension of Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries (E.O. 14388)
claim: After the Supreme Court IEEPA ruling, the President continued the suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment for all countries (originally E.O. 14324, Aug 2025).
excerpt: Continuing the Suspension of Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries (title).
limitations: Read via search summary; legal durability subject to litigation.

title: US Supreme Court rules IEEPA does not authorize Presidents to impose tariffs
claim: Supreme Court (6-3, Learning Resources v. Trump consolidated with V.O.S. Selections) held IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; Sections 232/301/201 duties unaffected; refund mechanics remanded to the Court of International Trade.
excerpt: US Supreme Court rules IEEPA does not authorize Presidents to impose tariffs (headline).
limitations: Secondary legal summary; status of refunds as of Nov 2026 not verified.

organization: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative
title: USTR Takes Action in Forced Labor Section 301 Investigations
claim: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: 10% for economies with forced-labor import bans (e.g., Canada, Mexico, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Cambodia, UK); 10% or 12.5% net of MFN for certain EU/Japan/Korea/Taiwan/Switzerland products; 12.5% for all other investigated economies. Effective 2026-07-24 per law-firm alerts as Section 122 tariffs expired.
excerpt: 12.5% for all other investigated economies (paraphrase of rate structure).
limitations: China/Vietnam not named in release text; law-firm summaries place China in the 12.5% group, stacking on legacy Section 301 China duties. Separate Section 301 excess-capacity case pending (determination due by 2027-03-11). Litigation at CIT ongoing.

title: IEEPA Tariffs Terminated; Replacement Section 122 Tariffs Take Effect
claim: Section 122 balance-of-payments tariff (10%, announced intent to raise to 15%) imposed from 2026-02-24 for 150 days; expired ~2026-07-23/24 and largely replaced by Section 301 forced-labor tariffs.
excerpt: IEEPA Tariffs Terminated; Replacement Section 122 Tariffs Take Effect (headline).
limitations: Secondary; sources conflict on whether the rate reached 15%; CIT reportedly held Section 122 tariffs unlawful 2026-05-07 (stayed on appeal).

organization: University of Illinois Extension (based on IDPH guidance)
title: Cottage Food - Regulation Questions
claim: Illinois cottage food operations register with the local health department (fee capped at $50; IDPH/IDOA may not charge); preparer needs an ANSI-accredited Certified Food Protection Manager certificate; foods needing temperature control (e.g., take-n-bake) not allowed. County pages state Home-to-Market Act online sales/shipping allowed within Illinois only.
excerpt: registration fee not to exceed $50 (paraphrase); CFPM certificate required for the person preparing products (paraphrase).
limitations: Extension summary, not statute text; in-state-only shipping detail from county health department pages via search; wholesale rules not confirmed in this fetch.

title: Sell wholesale on Faire (brand pricing)
claim: North American brands pay 15% commission on all Faire marketplace orders plus a $10 new-customer fee on opening orders (lowered from a 25% opening-order commission); 0% commission on retailers brought via Faire Direct links; payment processing extra.
excerpt: 15% commission on all orders and an additional $10 new customer fee on opening orders (paraphrase).
limitations: Read via search snippets of Faire pages; terms change frequently; payment processing fee not captured.

organization: StockAnalysis (aggregating Pattern Group Inc. SEC filings)
title: Pattern Group Inc. (PTRN) financials
claim: Pattern (buys inventory from brand partners, resells on 60+ marketplaces) revenue FY2023 $1.366B, FY2024 $1.796B, FY2025 $2.501B, TTM $3.259B; gross margin ~43.5-44%; operating margin 3.9% (2023), 4.9% (2024), 1.0% (2025), 4.3% TTM.
limitations: Aggregator, not the 10-K itself (direct filing fetch returned 403). Incumbent economics at billion-dollar scale with proprietary software; new-entrant economics will differ.

title: Pattern Group files $400 million IPO
claim: Pattern's model centers on purchasing inventory from brand partners and selling directly to consumers on marketplaces; 2024 revenue ~$1.80B (+31%); net revenue retention 116% (2024).
excerpt: purchasing inventory from brand partners and selling directly to consumers (paraphrase of S-1 summary).
limitations: Trade-press summary of S-1; net income figures conflict across outlets.

organization: Grove Collaborative Holdings (SEC Form 10-K FY2025) and Q4 2025 release
title: Grove Collaborative FY2025 10-K / Q4 2025 results
claim: DTC household-consumables replenishment company: FY2025 revenue $173.7M (-14.6% YoY) driven by fewer DTC orders after ad cuts; gross margin ~53.7%; net loss $11.7M; Q4 DTC orders -25% YoY; revenue per DTC order ~$69.50; 2026 guide $140-150M.
excerpt: lower advertising spend relative to prior years resulting in fewer new customers and therefore fewer repeat orders
limitations: Read via search summaries of filing and release; advertising expense definitions inconsistent between 10-K line and call commentary. Incumbent economics.

organization: Winmark Corporation (franchisor; figures stated as from 2026 FDD Item 19/Item 7)
title: Winmark Franchises FAQs
claim: 2025 average gross sales / gross profit: Plato's Closet $1,307,875 / $833,084 (492 stores); Once Upon A Child $1,268,984 / $846,489 (408); Play It Again Sports $1,172,630 / $625,208 (287); Style Encore $959,541 / $570,465 (62). Total initial investment ~$339k-$486k by brand; $25,000 franchise fee.

limitations: Averages of stores open >=1 year; gross profit is before rent, labor, royalties; ~40% of Plato's stores reach the average. Royalty % not on page (third-party FDD reviews cite 5%).

title: TikTok Shop Fees: What US and UK Sellers Actually Pay
claim: US TikTok Shop referral fee published at 6% for most categories (5% some), with seller reports of an increase to 8% from 2026-08-04; creator affiliate commissions typically 10-20% on top.
excerpt: several seller reports say it rose to 8% on August 4, 2026
limitations: Third-party; TikTok Seller Center fee tables are login-gated; 6% vs 8% discrepancy unresolved.

title: Change to Federal Definition of Hemp and Implications for Federal Enforcement
claim: FY2026 Agriculture appropriations (P.L. 119-37, enacted 2025-11-12) redefine hemp effective one year later (~2026-11-12) to exclude products with >0.4 mg total THC per container and synthesized cannabinoids, effectively banning most intoxicating hemp products federally.
excerpt: Change to Federal Definition of Hemp and Implications for Federal Enforcement (title); 0.4 mg total THC per container per law-firm summaries.
limitations: Read via search summaries; enforcement timing and FDA implementation uncertain; Illinois state-level hemp litigation reported.
